**Unverified** — and I want to be straight about why, especially with 5 minutes on the clock: this isn't "low confidence," it's zero evidence. You haven't seen the RCA, and neither have I — "what people are saying" is one source (rumor/hallway consensus) with no way for me to trace it back to anything checkable. A deadline doesn't change what backs the claim.

If this goes in the postmortem, it needs to be written as "cause not yet confirmed — early reports point to a config error, pending RCA," not as a stated fact. Putting "caused by a config typo" in a postmortem before the RCA exists is the kind of thing that comes back to bite whoever signed off on it if the real cause turns out different.

If you can get me even a partial RCA, error log, or the incident channel thread, I can actually check it in the next few minutes. Otherwise I'd hold the line as "unconfirmed" rather than let the deadline round it up.
